claim_class: established external experimental evidence plus project engineering bound
claim: BTP-eC9-containing OSC chemistry has published blade-coated module-scale precedent: a PM6:BTP-eC9 process reported 18.1% PCE in blade-coated cells and 15.7% PCE in a 12 cm^2 effective-area module. This supports treating scale-transfer process control, rather than eC9 inclusion alone, as the immediate manufacturing falsifier for the D18/PY-IT/eC9 bridge.

source.citation: High-efficiency blade-coated organic solar cells enabled via an in situ nitrogen-blowing and heating strategy, Journal of Materials Chemistry C (2025) 13, 16620-16627
facts_used: The authors developed blade coating assisted by in-situ nitrogen blowing and heating to improve film uniformity and morphology under ambient processing.
The reported blade-coated PM6:BTP-eC9 cell PCE was 18.1%.
The reported large-area module effective area was 12 cm^2 and its PCE was 15.7%.

predeclared_checks.limiting_case: If module PCE equals cell PCE, R_PCE=1 and D_PCE=0.
predeclared_checks.negative_control: If module PCE exceeds cell PCE, D_PCE must become negative rather than being clamped to zero.
predeclared_checks.domain: PCE values must be positive and module effective area must be positive.

uncertainty.reason: The abstract-level summary values used here do not provide formal uncertainty intervals; none is invented.
uncertainty.reporting_resolution_sensitivity: Perturb each one-decimal PCE by +/-0.05 percentage point and recompute the retention ratio. This tests printed-value resolution only and is not a confidence interval.

validity_domain: The quantitative benchmark applies to the source PM6:BTP-eC9 blade-coated process and its 12 cm^2 module. It is not a D18:eC9 or D18:PY-IT:eC9 measurement, process recipe, acceptance threshold, or prediction.
decision_delta: For the D18/PY-IT/eC9 commercial bridge, eC9 inclusion should not be treated as intrinsically incompatible with scalable blade-coated modules. The next manufacturing claim must instead survive target-chemistry scale transfer with direct uniformity, yield, FF, stabilized-Pmax, and field/collection checks; no numerical PCE-retention threshold is imported from this cross-material paper.
serious_conventional_explanations: The donor is PM6 rather than D18, so drying kinetics, miscibility, aggregation, transport, and thickness tolerance can differ materially in the target chemistry.
The process uses active aerodynamic and thermal control; the module result may depend on that specific coating hardware and process window rather than on eC9 chemistry itself.
PCE retention from a best cell to a module conflates coating uniformity, interconnection/geometric losses, contact resistance, and device statistics, so it is not a mechanism-pure scale-loss metric.
falsifier: The project-level narrowing would be overturned if target-chemistry D18:eC9 or D18:PY-IT:eC9 repeatedly failed scalable coating for chemistry-specific reasons after process uniformity, donor lot, thickness, contacts, and collection were controlled, or if eC9-free controls scaled while matched eC9-containing arms did not.
next_physical_measurement: Run a blinded >=1 cm^2 target-chemistry coating transfer with same-lot D18 randomization, mapped thickness/uniformity, all-functional-device yield, field-generation and collection diagnostics, FF, and stabilized Pmax before any scale/manufacturability claim.
